questions.promptHtml: Why is a fixed top-k with no similarity threshold dangerous in a RAG pipeline, and how do you choose a threshold?

sections.label: Why interviewers ask this
sections.html: It tests whether you understand that nearest neighbours always exist, and that bad context leads to confident wrong answers.

sections.label: 30-second answer
sections.html: Top-k always returns k results, even when none are relevant, so irrelevant chunks get pasted into the prompt, waste tokens and push the model toward wrong answers. A threshold lets the app say "nothing relevant found". But score scales differ per model and metric, so a threshold copied from a blog is wrong. I calibrate it on labelled queries, including questions that have no answer in the corpus, and I treat it as a per-model setting that I re-tune when the model changes.

sections.label: Deep explanation
sections.html:
Cosine scores are not probabilities. For one model, relevant matches might score 0.55 to 0.85 while irrelevant ones sit at 0.20 to 0.45; for another model the bands are different. So thresholds are model-specific and sometimes even query-length-specific.

Calibration method: build two sets, answerable queries (correct chunk exists) and unanswerable queries (nothing in the corpus). Retrieve top-1 for each and plot the score distributions. Choose a threshold that keeps most answerable queries while rejecting most unanswerable ones; decide which error costs more (missed answers or wrong answers).

Complementary tools: a reranker whose scores are better separated; a minimum number of results; dedupe and MMR; and an LLM instruction to answer "I don't know" when the context lacks the information. The code is the first gate; the prompt is the second.

sections.label: Code
sections.html:
def retrieve(q_vec, store, k=5, min_score=0.35):    # threshold must be tuned per model
    hits = store.search(q_vec, k)                   # [(text, score), ...]
    kept = [(t, s) for t, s in hits if s >= min_score]
    return kept or None                             # None = tell the user nothing relevant was found

def pick_threshold(answerable_top1, unanswerable_top1):
    # choose the score that maximises (answerable kept) - (unanswerable kept)
    best, best_t = -1, 0.0
    for t in sorted(set(answerable_top1 + unanswerable_top1)):
        gain = sum(s >= t for s in answerable_top1) / len(answerable_top1) \
             - sum(s >= t for s in unanswerable_top1) / len(unanswerable_top1)
        if gain > best: best, best_t = gain, t
    return best_t
fun filterHits(hits: List<Pair<String, Double>>, minScore: Double = 0.35): List<Pair<String, Double>>? =
    hits.filter { it.second >= minScore }.ifEmpty { null } // null = "no good match"; tune threshold per model

fun pickThreshold(ans: List<Double>, unans: List<Double>): Double =
    (ans + unans).distinct().sorted().maxByOrNull { t ->
        ans.count { it >= t }.toDouble() / ans.size - unans.count { it >= t }.toDouble() / unans.size
    } ?: 0.0
static List<String> filterHits(List<Map.Entry<String, Double>> hits, double minScore) {
    List<String> out = hits.stream().filter(h -> h.getValue() >= minScore).map(Map.Entry::getKey).toList();
    return out.isEmpty() ? null : out; // null = "no good match"; tune threshold per model
}

static double pickThreshold(List<Double> ans, List<Double> unans) {
    double best = -1, bestT = 0;
    for (double t : Stream.concat(ans.stream(), unans.stream()).distinct().sorted().toList()) {
        double gain = ans.stream().filter(s -> s >= t).count() / (double) ans.size()
                    - unans.stream().filter(s -> s >= t).count() / (double) unans.size();
        if (gain > best) { best = gain; bestT = t; }
    }
    return bestT;
}

sections.label: Common mistakes & traps
sections.html:
• Copying a threshold from a tutorial or another model.
  • Calibrating only on answerable queries.
  • One global threshold for very different query types.
  • Treating 0.9 as "90 percent relevant".

sections.label: Follow-ups
sections.html:
1. What if the threshold rejects too many good answers? → Lower it or add a reranker with better separation; look at the failing queries.
  2. Should I also threshold relative to the best score? → A relative cut (keep hits within some margin of the top score) helps when scores vary by query.
  3. How do you handle "I don't know" in the product? → Show a clear message plus a fallback (keyword search, ask to rephrase, human handoff) and log those queries to find content gaps.

sections.label: 3-YOE vs senior answer
sections.html: An average answer adds if score > 0.7. A senior calibrates on answerable and unanswerable sets, accounts for per-model scales, combines it with a reranker and "I don't know" prompting, and logs misses to find content gaps.

sections.label: Production connection
sections.html: A bot answered questions about a competitor product using unrelated chunks that scored 0.41; after calibrating a 0.5 threshold it replied "not covered" and the wrong-answer tickets dropped.
